title: Petra and the Ember
premise: Gideon Brightwater, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead, has spent his life in Emberfall, a valley warded so that magic—and the court beneath the mountain—cannot enter. When the wards collapse and the stars go dark, he learns his late sister's soul was sold to the Undercourt to buy the valley's protection, a bargain now called due. Guided by Petra, a runaway ward-keeper who betrayed her order to warn him, Gideon descends beneath the mountain to steal her soul back from the Ember itself. He succeeds only by trading his own silence—giving up the voices of the dead forever—and returns to rebuild the valley not as a refuge from magic, but as a home where truth and loyalty no longer have to be enemies.
about_author: Astrid Oyelaran is a former archivist who writes fantasy about quiet people in loud worlds, drawing on West African and Nordic folklore alike. She lives near a real mountain she refuses to go under.

chapters.title: The Valley That Magic Forgot
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. We meet Emberfall through his daily work: carving grave-tokens while the dead murmur their small regrets. His sister Wren died seven years ago; her voice is the one he can never find. Emotional beat: tender melancholy, a man at peace with being invisible.

chapters.title: Wren's Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The anniversary of Wren's death; their mother leaves her chair set as always. A stranger arrives at dusk asking about 'the debt of the valley.' Gideon lies for the first time in years. Beat: unease cracking routine.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The border wards fall with a sound like snapping harp strings; every star vanishes at once. The dead fall silent mid-sentence—the first true silence of his life. Beat: terror dressed as relief.

chapters.title: Petra at the Gate
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A wounded woman collapses at the ward-stones: Petra Vane, ward-keeper, deserter, carrying proof that Emberfall's protection was bought with a soul. She names Wren. Beat: reluctant alliance born of guilt.

chapters.title: What Mother Knew
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Confronting his mother, he learns the founders' bargain: one soul sold to the Undercourt each generation. Wren volunteered—or was chosen. Beat: betrayal inside family, love tangled with duty.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Souls
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the ruined ward-house they find the ledger; Wren's name is inked in ember-red, due for collection when the stars return. Petra confesses she helped forge the terms. Beat: trust tested by confession.

chapters.title: Voices in the Bone
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Desperate, he carves a token from Wren's old cradle-bone and finally hears her—a fragment, screaming, sold but not yet consumed. Beat: hope sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Road Down
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They leave the valley together, pursued by ward-hunters sent to erase witnesses. First journey beyond the borders either has known. Beat: wonder and fear braided; found-family spark ignites.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A river toll demands a memory as payment; Petra pays one of Gideon instead without asking. Their first fight. Beat: loyalty vs. honesty—she protected him by deceiving him.

chapters.title: Ashmarket
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A lawless town where souls are pawned like heirlooms. They hire Brannic, a disgraced underpriest who knows the mountain's doors. Beat: found family widens; the world is bigger and crueler than feared.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Kiss
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Ward-hunters corner them; Petra takes a wound meant for Gideon. In fever she reveals her full history—she was raised by the Undercourt as a tithe-child who escaped. Beat: vulnerability as intimacy.

chapters.title: Under the Mountain's Root
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They enter the deep roads guided by Brannic's stolen rites. The dead here are louder, angrier, older. Gideon realizes his gift may be a key. Beat: dread becoming purpose.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The Undercourt in all its candlelit horror: nobles wearing borrowed faces, including, briefly, Wren's. Petra must bow to the regent who once owned her name. Beat: old chains audibly clinking.

chapters.title: A Bargain of Faces
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. To move freely, Gideon trades three years of hearing the dead for a courtier's mask. Inside the mask he finds Wren's soul kept as a lamp-flame in the Ember vault. Beat: sacrifice begins; love against duty crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Regent's Offer
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The regent offers Wren's freedom if Gideon becomes the court's permanent bone-carver—replacing the voice it lost when Petra fled. Duty says accept; love refuses. Beat: the thematic fulcrum.

chapters.title: Brannic's Betrayal
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Brannic sells their plan to buy back his own priesthood. The vault route closes; Petra chooses to trust Gideon anyway and burns her keeper's oath-mark to open a forbidden way. Beat: loyalty chosen over safety.

chapters.title: Stealing the Flame
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The vault heist: Gideon carries Wren's flame in his own ribcage-carved lantern while the court wakes around them. The dead, grateful for his years of listening, rise to slow the guards. Beat: triumphant, costly escape.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At the mountain's mouth the regent blocks them: the flame cannot leave unless someone stays. Gideon prepares to remain—but the dead he freed claim the debt instead, taking the regent down with them. Beat: climax; grief and grace entwined.

chapters.title: Stars Returning
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Above ground, Wren's flame is released into the night sky; one star relights, then hundreds. Gideon hears her voice one last time—whole, forgiven, going home. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: What the Valley Owes
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They return to find Emberfall divided: some want the wards rebuilt, some want the truth buried. Petra stands before the council and tells everything, naming names, including her own. Beat: truth over comfort.

chapters.title: The Carving of New Names
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The valley votes to end the soul-bargain; new wards are cut from honest stone, powered by consent. Gideon, mostly deaf to the dead now, carves Wren's memorial token himself—at peace with silence. Beat: quiet transformation.

chapters.title: Ember and Morning
chapters.summary: Dual POV closing chapter. One year on: Petra trains a new generation of keepers bound by choice, not contract; Gideon teaches apprentices whose gifts are welcomed, not hidden. Found family gathered at Wren's chair, now filled by many. Beat: warm, earned resolution with an open door beneath the mountain.
